title: Git-style ids: threads, work packages and issues unique by construction
objective: Give every new steel thread, work package and issue an id that is unique by construction: derived from its creation event, minted on any branch, worktree or clone with no counter and no network, and never changed afterwards. Order every list by creation time. Keep every existing ordinal valid exactly as it is. Bring every door, view, document, skill, test and guard to the two forms, so that people and agents who share one repository through branches and merge requests never meet an id that means two things.
context: hv decision 61 (2026-11-19) rules the direction, at P0. An ordinal is minted highest-plus-one over the checked-out branch's canon, so it needs a single allocator, and a branch-and-merge flow has none: on an attendee's practice repository, one person with five merge requests open met a collision on every mint. ST0078 (2026-09-18) had rejected a change to the minting scheme and made renumber the repair. This thread reverses that line. vc reproduced the incident on brew 3.4.0 on 2026-11-19. The measurements, the design and the points still for hv are in `design.md`. No code lands before hv has reviewed this thread.

wps.title: Core tests take ids from the mint
wps.objective: Every test in intentsvcs and intentd takes a thread, work package or issue id from what the mint returned, so no test predicts the next number.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: S.

## Scope

- The facade's `st_new` already returns the id. `wp_new` and `issue_add` return a number today (`facade.rs:16174`, `19266`). Bind the return value at each site that today names the id it expects.
- dc's census classes P and H for these two crates (dc's census, section 4, banked under `refs/bank/dc/st0095/`). Class H is read one by one: a helper that mints, or a record a fixture seeded.
- A record a fixture seeded keeps its literal. That is class N, and it stays valid.

## Out of scope

- The tests whose subject is the ordinal scheme (`facade_st_wp.rs:22`, `:52`, `:91-92`, and the renumber and taken-id tests). They are rewritten with the scheme, in WP-06.
- intent-cli's tests (WP-02) and the shell (WP-03).

## Order

First, beside WP-02 and WP-03. Behaviour-neutral: it lands green on today's ordinals.

## Proof

The cut's own gate. dc's predict census over the two crates reads no site.

wps.title: The mint verbs say their id, and CLI tests read it
wps.objective: `st new`, `wp new` and `issues add` each say the id they minted in one machine-readable form, and every intent-cli test reads it from there.
wps.body:
Seat: ic. Size: M.

## Scope

- Today `st new` prints `created: ST0001`, and `issues add` prints `created: intent/.canon/issues/0001.json` and then `0001:<title>` (`cli_end_to_end.rs:128-133`, `212-218`). Neither has a machine form. Give the three verbs one, the same for all three. Its shape is ic's call (dc's census, section 2, banked under `refs/bank/dc/st0095/`).
- One capture helper in `intent-cli/tests/common/mod.rs`, beside `result_lines` (`:1184`), is the only place a CLI test learns a minted id.
- Convert intent-cli's tests that predict a mint: 54 files drive the binary's mints.
- Regenerate `docs/reference` in the commit that changes help or the register, or the cut's reference gate refuses.

## Out of scope

- `cli_end_to_end.rs:128-133`, `169-171` and `212-218`, which assert the ordinal scheme itself. They change in WP-10.

## Order

First, beside WP-01 and WP-03. Behaviour-neutral.

## Proof

The cut's own gate.

wps.title: The commit gate spares the main store; scripts capture ids
wps.objective: The repository's commit gate never migrates the main checkout's store, every script and bats file that mints reads the id from the mint's output through one shell function, and the two cut steps that predict ST0001 stop predicting.
wps.body:
Seat: dc. Size: M.

## Scope

- First, and before any other package lands: the commit gate judges a copy of the store whenever the build's store schema is newer than the store's. The gate runs the dev binary's `doctor` on the store of the checkout that is committing (`bin/.devbin/cmd/precommit:302-330`, `thread_view_skew_check.sh:84`), and every seat shares that build target, so without this the first commit after WP-06 lands migrates the main store and brew 3.4.0 then refuses it.
- One shell function in `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/`, which the devbin commands and bats already source. It reads WP-02's machine form.
- The brew smoke (`bin/.devbin/cmd/brew:80`, `370-371`, `392`) requires the output to name ST0001 and then triages ST0001. It runs after publish, so a failure lands once the release is public. It is fixed here, before the rehearsal.
- The explorer screenshots (`gen_explorer_shots.sh:140-163`, `194`) name ST0001, its work packages 01 to 03 and `ST0003/wp/01`. Capture the ids, and seed fixed ids for the demo so two runs still write byte-identical images (issue 0623).
- No bats file mints today. Keep it so.

## Out of scope

- The scripts that carry an id pattern. They change in WP-12, once the waist's read door exists.

## Order

First, beside WP-01 and WP-02. The function follows WP-02's machine form.

## Proof

The brew smoke and the screenshot step run green on today's ordinals, and the screenshots are byte-identical across two runs. For the gate: a commit made with a build whose store schema is newer leaves the checkout's store at its own schema.

wps.title: The waist: one module owns an id
wps.objective: One module, `intentsvcs::id`, owns the ordinal id end to end behind typed ids, with every site in the workspace routed through it and no behaviour changed.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: L.

## Scope

- Register `intentsvcs::id` in `intent/llm/MODULES.md` first. It absorbs `model.rs`'s id section (`:55-60`, `:124-254`, `:296-509`).
- `ThreadId`, `WpId` and `IssueId`, each over one form that is an ordinal today and can hold a hash later, with no constructor outside the module. They replace `Thread.id: String` (`model.rs:564`), `WorkPackage.seq: u32` (`:1009`), `Issue.number: u32` (`:2065`) and `Related.id` (`:974`).
- Every site the compiler then lists: about 70 hand formatters in 17 files (ic's census, section 1, banked under `refs/bank/ic/st0095/`), the store's numeric bindings, ingest, export, renumber and doctor (cc's census, section 4, banked under `refs/bank/cc/st0095/`), and intent-cli's `render.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `show.rs` and `tui/app.rs`. cc converts the whole workspace in this one unit, and ic reads intent-cli's part.
- The module's duties in `design.md`, "One home: the waist", for the ordinal family: one stored-form reader, the pure operator reader, one formatter with each rendered form, one order, one text scanner in place of three, and the forms sentence.
- Two duplicates go first: the fiat cascade's inline copy of `contract::group_of` (`facade.rs:19703-19710`), and an issue's search owner spelled `703` (`ingest.rs:1859`) where everything else spells `0703`.
- The 37 test files that pass a number where an id is meant change type with it.

## Out of scope

- Any new family, any format change in the canon or the store, any new verb.

## Order

After WP-01, and before everything else of cc's.

## Proof

Today's suite passes unchanged through the cut's own gate, and an existing project's `intent sync` plans nothing after the build. `legacy.rs` calls the ordinal predicate and never a widened one.

wps.title: The merge knows both families
wps.objective: A merge between branches that each minted is resolved by `intent sync --apply --yes` alone, with no record discarded and no file left to a person that Intent can merge exactly.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: S, down from M when cc dropped the `.intentfiles` set merge on 2026-11-19.

## Scope

- `plan.rs` `classify` (`:608-708`) owns a hashed record's canon, sidecars and realised directory. Today any canon path that is not an ordinal goes to take-a-side, which discards one side's record. Two hashed adds never go there.
- Two branches that each add a work package to one thread: their ids differ, so both are kept (`:529-567`), with no renumber and no moved claim.
- Not here: `.intentfiles` and the two aggregate views. ST0096 takes all three out of git, so this package neither merges `.intentfiles` as a set nor regenerates the lists. A merge of two branches both still in today's format meets the conflict it meets today, and `intent upgrade` is that state's one remedy. Issue 0704 is superseded by ST0096, and AC-05.2 is withdrawn with that reason (cc, 2026-11-19).
- The transition: an ordinal both sides minted before the upgrade is repaired by moving this clone's record to a hashed id, from its own creation event where the log holds one, and from an event the repair mints where it does not. `next_free_id` (`facade.rs:12153-12214`) and issue 0555's seq arithmetic retire. The mover is today's `land_renumber` (`facade.rs:15375-15567`), and it is what `st remint` and `issues remint` call.
- Two defects in the merge path go with it: `issue_seq(..).unwrap_or(0)` (`facade.rs:12658-12661`), and `path.starts_with(old)` with no `/` guard (`:12702-12705`).

## Order

After WP-04. Its `classify` change lands in the same unit as WP-06's mint: a mint that lands first loses a record at the first merge.

## Proof

The two-clone rig (`two_clones_that_mint_one_id_are_repaired_by_renumber.rs`), driven for each case above.

wps.title: The hashed family
wps.objective: Every new thread, work package and issue is minted as a hashed id derived from its creation event, the canon and the store carry it, and no verb mints an ordinal again.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: L.

## Scope

- The mint: the event envelope first, then the id as its marker plus the front of `sha256_hex(origin)`: 16 hex for a thread and an issue, 8 for a work package. It refuses an id this clone can see (the store, the canon directory, the realised directory, and the ids taken in a plan), and it draws a new event id when the new short form equals that of a visible record of its own kind. The draw is inside the one mint, happens before anything is written, and is bounded: after its last draw the mint refuses loudly. Its test uses a real pair of ULIDs whose hashes share a short form, found by search and kept as a fixture.
- Canon: `number` and `seq` become `id`; `origin` goes on a thread, a work package and an issue, written for hashed records only; the thread and issue schemas take a new version.
- The store goes from schema 35 to 36 with two table rebuilds: `issues.number` is the rowid (`store.rs:332-333`), and `wps.seq` is an integer (`:255-275`).
- `intent upgrade` gains the canon format migration: byte-deterministic, over every issue file and every thread file with a work package, with no id changed.
- The stored-form reader refuses a canon name of neither family by name. That ends the silent skip (`project.rs:2645-2661`, inherited at `migrate.rs:358-373` and `ingest.rs:370`).
- The faces and the export bundle take their new versions with ic. WP-10 carries the GraphQL side.
- The tests whose subject is the ordinal scheme are rewritten here: `facade_st_wp.rs`, and the two-clone test, which becomes the proof.

## Order

After WP-05, as one unit with its `classify` change.

## Proof

The two-clone test: two clones, and two worktrees, each mint a thread, a work package in one shared thread, and an issue from one base, and merge with different ids and no repair.

wps.title: Prefix resolution
wps.objective: One resolver turns what a person typed into the one record it names, or says which records it could name, and nothing stored is ever a prefix.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: M.

## Scope

- `resolve.rs` (`:92-135`) takes a spelling and the project's ids, and returns the id, the candidates of an ambiguous prefix, or not found. It is the only place a prefix is expanded, for the CLI, the TUI and MCP.
- An ordinal-shaped spelling is always the ordinal. A hash prefix is at least 4 hex characters.
- The facade's verbs take typed ids. Claims (`facade.rs:11454`, `11477`), `events --subject` (`:7138`) and `Scope::selects` (`sync.rs:411-418`) resolve before they compare, and keep comparing whole ids.
- The pure spelling stays pure: MCP validates its arguments with no store (`mcp.rs:1915`).

## Order

After WP-06.

## Proof

The waist's own tests, with hashed records seeded through the fixture writer, two that share a short form among them.

wps.title: The order
wps.objective: Every listing orders ordinals by number and hashed records by creation, in its present buckets and direction, so a project of ordinals renders exactly as it does today.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: S.

## Scope

- One comparator in the waist, keyed on the id's family: ordinals first, by number; hashed records after, by `origin`.
- The store's reads that order by id or number today: `ORDER BY id` (`store.rs:5083`), issues `ORDER BY number` (`:5156-5164`) and work packages `ORDER BY seq` (`:5240-5244`); and the text sorts in ingest (`ingest.rs:1041`, `1144-1150`) and migrate (`migrate.rs:447`).
- Criteria and tests keep `id_order` in canon. `acceptance.md`'s group order follows the package order.

## Order

After WP-06. ic applies the comparator to the views in WP-10.

## Proof

`tests/unit/output_width.bats` and the view goldens are unchanged for a project of ordinals.

wps.title: Criteria follow their package, and doctor verifies
wps.objective: A hashed work package's criteria and tests are found by its id at every site that reads the group, and doctor proves each hashed id against the event that made it.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: S.

## Scope

- The group of a criterion or test id is its package's id. Four places read it: the close gate (`contract.rs:19-33`, `59-65`), `wp show` and `wp gate` (`facade.rs:5582-5590`), `acceptance.md` (`views.rs:1301-1318`) and doctor (`doctor.rs:820-830`, `1244-1258`, `1427-1431`).
- The gate's roll-up (`contract.rs:888-896`): when no criterion matches a package's group, the gate passes. A hashed package whose criteria carry its group must be judged by them. This is the riskiest site in the census.
- Doctor: `verify(id, origin)`; a duplicate id keyed by the typed id (`doctor.rs:1094-1123`); a canon name of neither family; and an advisory, not counted, that names two records of one kind whose short forms are the same.
- Check how search stems a hex token before search is relied on for ids.

## Order

After WP-06.

## Proof

A test that `wp done` refuses a hashed package with an unsatisfied criterion of its own.

wps.title: Every door takes and shows both families
wps.objective: Every door a person or an agent uses takes an id of either family or a unique prefix, shows a hashed id by its short form, and carries the whole id wherever one is stored.
wps.body:
Seat: ic. Size: L.

## Scope

- The CLI's parsers, and the length rule in the pure spelling. Each door resolves through WP-07, and refuses an ambiguous prefix with each candidate's id, kind, title and created date.
- Both path grammars go through the type: `intent:///` and the navigator's `/thread/<id>/wps/<seq>` (`nav.rs:204-307`).
- Claim, manifest and URI forms, and a criterion's group, take a prefix at the door and store the whole id.
- Tables: the shown form, an id column that floors at its content width (`views.rs:156`), and a Created column on the issues table (`render.rs:1051`). The views' headings and frontmatter, eg `WP-c2e4`. ic applies WP-08's comparator to the two thread orders (`views.rs:1454`, `:1696`) and the two issue orders (`facade.rs:5393`, `views.rs:1465`).
- GraphQL: `issue(number: Int!)`, `Issue.number` and `WorkPackage.seq` become `id: String!` with no alias (`schema.graphql:349`, `:428`, `:818`), with a creation instant added. The faces take their new version with cc.
- MCP's descriptions (`mcp.rs:277-329`), the dispatch table's help, and the remedy texts (`facade.rs:3479`, `intentfiles.rs:370`, `intentd/src/store.rs:860-878`) quote the waist's forms sentence.
- `st remint <id>` and `issues remint <id>`, with their dispatch rows (`dispatch-table.json:1244-1284`), replace the two renumber verbs. The old two-argument call is refused with its remedy.
- One read door on the binary for scripts: is this token an id, of which kind, and which record does it name.
- The CLI tests whose subject is the ordinal scheme (`cli_end_to_end.rs:128-133`, `169-171`, `212-218`), and the regenerated guide and `docs/reference`.

## From the Highlander sweep (vc decision 133)

vc's sweep of the existing code is banked at `refs/bank/vc/st0095/highlander-B-rust-rest-20261119`, and its clusters are the anchors. Each goes through the waist (WP-04) and cc's operator reader (WP-07):

- D1: a work package's id is formatted inline at 19 sites (`render.rs` 10, `mcp.rs` 8, `show.rs:94`) with no formatter. Every site takes the waist's.
- D2: one work package has six display spellings (`mcp.rs:2072` emits `.../wp/1`, which a test pins, where `facade.rs:16505` emits `.../wp/01`). Each rendered form has one spelling, from that formatter.
- D3: the issue id's `{:04}` is inline at 15 sites, `model::issue_id` has no caller in scope, and the CLI says "issue 0021" where MCP says "0021". One formatter and one wording.
- D4: `<thread>/<NN>` is parsed in five places under three rules (`render.rs:10027`, `scope_of`, takes `+3` and `003` and turns `ST0001/abc` into a thread id). One operator reader.
- D5: doors that skip the thread door: `todo done`, `todo notdone` and `todo toggle`, `ac descope --to`, `events --subject`, and MCP's `ac list`, `at list` and `at lint`, which drop the `/NN` the CLI passes on. Every one goes through the door. Issue 0713 records the live defects.
- D6: bad-id refusals have three homes (`mcp.rs:1914` folds every `IdError` into one message, and `render.rs:16444` uses `THREAD_DIGITS` for issues and spells the `s` and `i` tags beside `IdKind::tag()`). One refusal, quoting the waist's sentence of forms.
- D7 to D10: entity header lines restated for MCP resource names, worked-example ids, criterion and test label handling, and an `Address` for this project built by hand. Each goes to its one home.
- The dispatch table declares an id type for every argument, and `render.rs` picks its reader from that declaration, not one per arm.
- `intent set`, and every door that takes a work package, takes the `<thread>/<package>` form `wp new` prints (dc, 2026-11-19: `intent set ST0001/01 objective` is refused today).
- intent-cli's test helpers (T1 to T9: `.intentfiles` parsed by hand, minimal canon written by hand, worked-example ids as scattered literals) become one set in `tests/common`, on the waist's types. WP-02 left a minted id to `common::created` alone. The tests that search rendered output for a captured id take its shown form here, or their negative checks pass for nothing once the shown form is shorter than the stored one.

## Order

After WP-02 and WP-07. Its doors can accept both families before WP-06 mints one.

## Proof

The cut's own gate, with hashed records seeded through the fixture writer.

wps.title: The TUI, the app and the served page
wps.objective: The TUI lists, opens and moves between hashed threads, work packages and issues, and the app and the served page show them.
wps.body:
Seat: ic. Size: M.

## Scope

- The TUI's source formats ids from `number` and `seq` (`render.rs:7350`, `:7630`, `:7791-7808`; `tui/views.rs:298`; `outstanding.rs:134`, `:166`). The navigator re-spells a work package through a number, so `0712` becomes `712` (`nav.rs:584`). The loaders parse numbers (`facade.rs:5502`, `:5548`, `:5577`). Two forms declare number widgets (`forms.json:173`, `:232`).
- The omnibox ranks a complete id or a unique prefix first.
- The Swift app holds ids as opaque strings: it needs one hashed fixture.
- The served page: its refusal examples name both families (`intentd/src/store.rs:864`, `:870`), and its `shortId`, which keeps a tail, is not used for ids.

## Order

After WP-10.

## Proof

The cut's own gate, and the explorer screenshots regenerated in the cut's own step.

wps.title: The pipeline asks the waist; the drill; the fleet
wps.objective: No script, hook, template or workflow carries a pattern for an id, this repository has carried hashed records through its own gates before the cut, and each estate knows what its upgrade is.
wps.body:
Seat: dc. Size: M.

## Scope

- Each of these asks WP-10's read door in place of its own pattern: `pr-checks.yml:35`, `:37`; `session-context.sh:47` with `_wip.md:7`, which reads the first bold focus line with no id pattern; `rulings_check.sh:194`; `declared_kind_check.sh:175`, `:200`; and `canon-ignore-guard.sh:78-79`, which probes the names the waist gives it. Their bats tests change with them.
- A guard in the commit gate refuses a new id pattern in a script, hook, template or skill. In Rust the type is the guard.
- The by-hand ST0056 instruments (dc's census, section 3, items 8, 9 and 11, banked under `refs/bank/dc/st0095/`) are not routed: dc proposes their retirement separately. Items 10 and 12 scan v2 estates, which hold only ordinals, and need no change.
- The drill: in a clone of this repository upgraded with the new build, mint a hashed thread, work package and issue, and commit them through the whole commit gate, with doctor and the pull-request check passing.
- The fleet's note, for the visit hv decision 41 already plans: every machine upgrades first; `intent upgrade`; `intent claude upgrade --apply`; and a read-only grep for a hand-copied `pr-checks.yml`.

- From vc's Highlander sweep of the existing code (report C, `refs/bank/vc/st0095/highlander-C-non-rust-20261119`), folded in by dc:
  - The five gated tools that join a canon name, an id and a realised directory by string concatenation ask the binary for the join instead: `absent_at_check.sh:170`, `declared_kind_check.sh:135`, `:294`, `stale_at_check.sh:126-127`, `rulings_check.sh:191-206` and `canon_commit_check.sh:165-176`, which takes its labels from `.id` and its directories from the file name. So WP-10's read door also answers, for an id, its canon file and its realised directory (cluster C).
  - The gate's other shapes go the same way: `rulings_check.sh:167-215` (an issue as three or four digits), `rulings_check.sh:203` (`WP/[0-9][0-9]/info.md`) and `view_skew_check.sh:241` (the `ST` prefix) (clusters D, E and F).
  - `stale_at_check.sh:177-210` reads its AT rows from canon, as `absent_at_check.sh` and `declared_kind_check.sh` already do, instead of re-parsing the rendered `acceptance.md` (cluster G).
  - `thread_view_skew_check.sh:130`, `:134` read doctor's summary and residue lines as text, a workaround that tool's own header dates. They read doctor's machine form once doctor has one (cluster I).
  - `canon_ignore_guard.bats:102`, whose ignore rule `intent/.canon/st/ST9*` holds only because the guard's probe starts with `ST9`, changes with the guard (cluster K).
  - This repository's fixtures spell a work package `ST0001/WP-01` (`tests/unit/whiteboard_header_guard.bats:379`, `:390` and `tests/fixtures/whiteboard-header/laksa-ic-a0077c605.md:9`), and take the one spelling. The docs' spellings are WP-13's (cluster F).
  - The dead `st_prefix` key leaves `intent/.config/config.json:33`, which nothing has read since `dispatch.rs:81-89`, and its copy in `critic_global_rig.sh:96` goes with it (cluster D).
  - The by-hand probes that assume the mint read the id through `minted_id`, or retire with the by-hand instruments: `canon_race_check.sh:104-108`, `read_claim_probe.sh:76-77`, `inert_arg_check.sh:99`, `:133-138`, `sync_issue_loss.sh:45`, `:64-65`, `fixture_probe.sh:225-227`, `:249` and `no_daemon_required.sh:166-179` (cluster H).
  - dc's retirement proposal also takes `realise_plan.sh` (its manifest grammar, declaration rule and `printf '%04d'`) and ST0057's `sparse_tree_equals_manifest.sh`, which refuses this repository's own manifest. No gate, CI step or bats test runs either (clusters A, B and E).

## Order

After WP-03 and WP-10. The drill runs before the rehearsal.

## Proof

The drill itself.

wps.title: Docs, skills, rules and templates teach the new ids
wps.objective: Every page, skill, rule and template that teaches an id teaches both families, how to type one, and what a project does on upgrade.
wps.body:
Seat: ac, or ic if hv does not start ac. Size: L.

## Scope

- About 90 teaching lines and 221 example lines across 21 files (ic's census, section 1, banked under `refs/bank/ic/st0095/`0).
- `docs/concepts/working-in-a-team.md`: the five collision sections are rewritten from a drive of the new build, the five-open-merge-requests shape among them, and a new section says what a shared short form is and what the door says about it.
- The shipped skills (`in-essentials`, `in-whiteboard`, `in-plan`), two rules, one subagent, `_AGENTS.md`, and `_wip.md`.
- An upgrade note: every machine first; `intent upgrade` once per project; an open branch upgrades before it merges; and nothing is renumbered.

- The 21 reference pages, `cut-surface.md` and the screenshots regenerate in the cut's own steps, and are not written by hand.
- From the Highlander sweep (vc decision 133, report C at `refs/bank/vc/st0095/highlander-C-non-rust-20261119`): `intent/docs/working-with-llms.md:506` copies the claim-forms sentence and no test holds the copy, so it quotes or points at the waist's sentence of forms instead. The dispatch table's help strings feed `--help`, the guide and `docs/reference`, so a form taught there is written once, in the table.

## Order

The forms are fixed by this design, so drafting starts at hv's review. The transcripts are driven once WP-10 has landed.

## Proof

Every command on every changed page has been driven on the new build.

wps.title: Kind tags and the owner of a path have one home
wps.objective: The id families have one set of kind tags, with one wire spelling for each surface, and one answer to which thread or issue owns a path, so no caller names a family or claims a path by its own copy.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: S. Lands after WP-04, alongside WP-06. cc split it from WP-04 on 2026-11-19 (cc's "WP-04b") so that WP-04 lands sooner, since WP-05 and WP-06 do not need it.

## Scope

- **Kind tags.** At least eight enums or string sets name the id families today, and a work package is spelled `wp`, `work-package`, `work_package` and `work package` (the Highlander sweep, report A, cluster C11). One enum in the waist, with one wire spelling for each surface. That fixes issue 0708, where `search --kind wp` never finds a work package's prose because ingest writes `work-package` and `HitKind::of_owner` maps only `wp` and `work_package`.
- **Which record owns a path.** There are six answers today (report A, cluster C6). One function answers it, and every caller asks it.
- **The dead `st_prefix` key** in this project's `intent/.config/config.json`. Nothing reads it but legacy's retired-setting warning, which is silent for `ST`. It is removed.

## Out of scope

- The id concerns WP-04 takes, the mint (WP-06) and the order (WP-08).

## Proof

# ST0095: Design. Git-style ids for threads, work packages and issues

**Status: under way since 2026-11-19 09:38Z by vc's date -u, on hv's go (hv decision 65). hv decision 66 adds ST0096 beside it and hv decision 67 the Highlander check.** hv decisions 61 to 64 rule the direction and the two forks the seats raised. Written by vc from its own measurements and from the read-only census cc, ic and dc each made of their remit the same day. A claim says whether it was measured or read. The three censuses are banked under `refs/bank/cc/st0095/`, `refs/bank/ic/st0095/` and `refs/bank/dc/st0095/`, and vc's reproduction under `refs/bank/vc/st0095/`; an anchor in a work package comes from them. The points still open are under "For hv at review".

## The rulings

hv, 2026-11-19, in hv's words unless marked:

- "We need to go all-in a fix to ST, WP, and ISSUE numbering (from ordinals to git-style hashes based on the guid of the creation event). This is a P0 fix that needs to be done asap." (decision 61)
- "Everywhere, going forward." Lists order by "date/time ... rather than ordinally". A stop-gap that restricts where a record may be created: "We can't have that restriction." (61)
- "In this case we DO NEED TO BE BACKWARDS COMPATIBLE with the old ordinal style numbering. And we need to ensure that we highlander both the minting of these new ids and any checks on them into as tight a waist as possible." (62)
- Other ordinals count only "if they are subject to the same issues as STs, WPs, and Issues". (62)
- **The stored id is long, and the short form is how it is shown and typed, as in git.** hv chose cc's position over the first draft. cc's words: "the stored id must be long enough never to collide, and the 7 characters are how it is shown and typed, as in git." (64)
- **Criterion and test ids stay caller-assigned**, and only their group follows the work package's id. (64)
- Whiteboard item numbers stay out. Issue 0705 gets its own thread in the same release, ST0096. (63, 66)

This reverses one line of ST0078's design (2026-09-18): "Rejected: changing the minting scheme."

## Why: what was measured

**The incident.** On an attendee's practice repository, one person had five merge requests open for review at once. Each new thread was minted from main and took a number an open merge request already held, four times running. One issue number collided the same way. Each was repaired by hand with `intent st renumber` or `intent issues renumber`.

**The reproduction** (vc, brew 3.4.0, a scratch repository under an isolated HOME, a second clone standing in for the forge's merge button):

| What was driven                                        | What happened                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `intent st new` on main while a branch holds ST0003    | ST0003 again, every time: the post-checkout hook had taken the branch's thread out of the store      |
| `intent issues add` on a branch while another has 0002 | 0002 again                                                                                           |
| All six branches merged in order, renumbered as above  | `intent doctor` 0 findings, in the working clone and in a fresh clone                                |
| `intent events --subject ST0003` on the merged result  | Five `st.new` events, one of them real; each renumbered thread's history starts at its `st.renumber` |
| The forge merging the second branch after the first    | Refused: conflicts in `intent/.intentfiles`, `intent/st/steel_threads.md` and `intent/todo.md`       |
| `intent sync --apply --yes` in that conflicted merge   | Refused (rc 1) until `.intentfiles` is resolved by hand; then it regenerates both views              |

**Why ST0078's answer does not hold.** ST0078 kept highest-plus-one and made renumber the repair, reading a collision as a rare race between two people. In a review-gated flow it is the steady state: one person with several merge requests open collides on every mint. hv's own estates never met it because every seat mints in the one main checkout, against one store, and commits straight to main. That checkout is a single allocator. A merge-request flow has none.

**The structural reason.** A sequential number needs one allocator, and git has none until the merge. Any number handed out on a branch is a guess about what the merge will find.

## The principle

**An id is minted where its record is born, from nothing but that birth, and it never changes.** No counter, no network, no restriction on where a mint may run. Two mints are never asked to agree, because neither reads anything the other writes.

## What an id is

### The definition (cc's, as the id's meaning)

Every mint already writes a creation event, and every event already has a globally unique id: a ULID from the crate's one minter (`event::next_id`, `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/event.rs:381`). The creation ops are `st.new`, `wp.new` and `issues.add`.

**A new id is its kind's marker followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its creation event's id, cut from the front.** The digest is `model::sha256_hex` over the event id exactly as `next_id` returns it. There is no second hasher and no second source of randomness.

The record carries the creation event's id in a new canon field, `origin`. The id is derived from it and never stored beside it as a second fact: `doctor` verifies that a hashed id is its marker plus the front of `sha256(origin)`. Each creation verb mints its event envelope first and derives the id from it, the order the fiat cascade already uses (`facade.rs:19790`).

### Stored, shown, typed

| Form       | A thread and an issue               | A work package, in its thread | Where it is used                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Stored** | marker + 16 hex                     | 8 hex                         | Canon file names, realised directories, `.intentfiles` rows, claims, `related`, criterion groups, event subjects, URIs |
| **Shown**  | marker + the first 7                | the first 4                   | Every table, view and message. Fixed, so a committed view is the same bytes on every branch                            |
| **Typed**  | any unique prefix of at least 4 hex | the same                      | Every door, with or without the marker, in any case                                                                    |

- **Sixty-four bits do not collide.** So nothing ever moves a hashed record, and no repair is written for one.
- **A shared short form is an ambiguity, never a misdirection.** The door refuses it and lists each candidate with its kind, title and created date. With a 7-character stored id, the repair would move one record, and every short reference already written on its branch would then name the other record with no error. That is today's defect made rarer, and it is why hv chose the long stored id.
- **The mint keeps short forms apart.** It refuses an id equal to one this clone can see, which at 64 bits never fires. It also draws a new creation event id when the new short form equals that of a visible record of its own kind: before anything is written, inside the one mint, and a bounded number of times before it refuses loudly. Without that, a project of 3,000 ids would have about a 1 in 60 chance of two rows showing one short form. With it, two rows share one only if two branches that have not met minted them: about 4 in 10 million per mint, with 100 records in flight. `doctor` then names both as an advisory, and nothing moves.
- **Nothing stored is a prefix.** Claims, `related`, criterion groups and event subjects compare exact strings today, and they stay correct only if what is stored is whole.

### The forms, by kind

| Kind            | Ordinal form: existing, and valid for ever | Hashed form, stored                         | Shown       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| Thread          | `ST0092`                                   | `ST3f9a2c1d4e5f6a7b`                        | `ST3f9a2c1` |
| Issue           | `0703`                                     | `I3f9a2c1d4e5f6a7b`                         | `I3f9a2c1`  |
| Work package    | `ST0092/09`                                | `ST3f9a2c1d4e5f6a7b/c2e41a0b`               | `WP-c2e4`   |
| Criterion, test | `AC-09.3`, caller-assigned                 | `AC-c2e41a0b.3`, the group its package's id | `AC-c2e4.3` |

- **Every hashed id carries a kind marker** (cc, as meaning, and dc from the pipeline): bare hex can be an English word or a plausible file name, three places rely on an id not looking like a word (`intentfiles.rs:38-42`, `legacy.rs:3366`, `contract.rs:267-283`), and `organize` removes a file in `intent/issues/` that it takes for an undeclared view. ic first preferred a bare issue id and withdrew it on cc's evidence. The letters are ic's: a thread is `ST` plus hex, an issue is `I` plus hex, and a work package takes no letter, because it never stands alone.
- **No spelling is both an ordinal and a hash.** An ordinal is at most 4 decimal digits (2 for a work package). Anything longer is a hash or its prefix.
- **An existing ordinal thread gains hashed work packages** from the switch on, so one thread carries both families: `ST0094/01` beside `ST0094/c2e41a0b`.
- A branch or ref takes the lowercase id, as the estate's refs do today.

### Order

**The key is the id's family.** Ordinals come first, by number: that is the order they were minted in, and the order they have today. Hashed records follow, by `origin`, whose first 48 bits are the minting millisecond. Each list keeps its present buckets and direction.

So a project that holds only ordinals renders every view exactly as it does now, and no committed view in any estate re-renders on upgrade. `created` cannot be the key: it is a date with no time, and a work package has none.

### Typing an id

- **An ordinal-shaped spelling is always the ordinal.** `46`, `0046`, `ST46`, `ST0046`, `s46` and `i21` keep today's meaning.
- **Anything else of at least 4 hex characters is a hash prefix**, and one made only of digits needs 5. The pure half of this is ic's length rule; which record a prefix names is decided once, against the store, in `resolve.rs`, for the CLI, the TUI and MCP.
- An ambiguous prefix is refused with its candidates, and none is picked.
- Every answer prints the id's shown form, and `--json` and the canon carry the stored one.
- **The one bend in backwards compatibility**: today leading zeros are trimmed, so `00046` reaches ST0046. A five-digit token is a hash prefix now, so that spelling stops. hv accepted the bend (hv decision 70).

### Existing ordinals: backwards compatible, by hv's ruling

**Every existing id stays exactly as it is, for ever, and keeps working at every door.** No record is renumbered, no alias is added, no history or prose is rewritten, and the event log's subjects stay as written. Both families live in one project, one table and one grammar. After the upgrade no verb mints an ordinal again, in any project.

This is a standing exception to "fail forward, no shims", on hv's word: accepting the ordinal form is a permanent part of the id.

**Ordinals already in flight.** A branch cut before the upgrade can still carry an ordinal that collides when it merges. `intent sync --apply --yes` repairs it by moving this clone's record to a hashed id, derived from its own creation event where the log holds one. `st remint <id>` and `issues remint <id>` do the same by hand, with one argument, and replace `st renumber` and `issues renumber`. `next_free_id`'s arithmetic retires.

### One home: the waist

**One module, `intentsvcs::id`, owns an id end to end, and nothing outside it makes, reads, writes, scans or checks one.** It absorbs `model.rs`'s id section and is registered in `intent/llm/MODULES.md` before it is written.

1. **Types.** `ThreadId`, `WpId` and `IssueId`, each an ordinal or a hash, with no constructor outside the module. They replace `Thread.id: String`, `WorkPackage.seq: u32` and `Issue.number: u32`. A `{:04}` then does not compile against an id, so the compiler lists every site: about 70 hand formatters in 17 files today (ic's count).
2. **One mint**, called by `st new`, `wp new`, `issues add` and the transition's re-mint, and nowhere else.
3. **One stored-form reader**, for canon names and contents, `.intentfiles`, claims, `related`, addresses, event subjects and realised paths. It refuses by name anything that is neither family.
4. **One operator reader**: the pure spelling, and `resolve` above it.
5. **One formatter**: the stored form, the shown form, and each rendered form a surface needs (claim, manifest row, path stem, URI segment, `WP-` heading, lowercase ref).
6. **One order**: the family key above.
7. **One text scanner** for "which ids does this text name", replacing three (`legacy.rs:3366`, `contract.rs:267-283`, `contract.rs:351-359`).
8. **One check**: `verify(id, origin)`, for `doctor`.
9. **One sentence of forms** that every refusal, help string, MCP description and the guide quote, in place of today's hand-spelled copies.
10. **One read door on the binary** for scripts: is this token an id, of which kind, and which record does it name. No shell guard, hook, template or workflow carries a pattern of its own, and a guard in the commit gate holds that for everything the compiler cannot see.

## What changes

### The model, the canon and the store (cc)

- **Canon.** `Issue.number` and `WorkPackage.seq` become a string `id`; `origin` is added to a thread, a work package and an issue, written for hashed records only. The thread and issue schemas take a new version, and every canon struct stays `deny_unknown_fields`.
- **The upgrade rewrites the canon's format once.** `intent upgrade` turns `703` into `"0703"` and `1` into `"01"` in every issue file and every thread file with a work package. It is byte-deterministic, so a branch upgraded on its own merges cleanly with main upgraded on its own. It changes no id. This is new work in `intent upgrade`, which rewrites nothing today.
- **Why eager and not as files are next written**: an older binary refuses a canon file by its schema's name and reads nothing, which is the only thing that stops it. Brew 3.4.0 silently skips an issue file whose name is not a decimal number and then deletes it (`project.rs:2645-2661`, `store.rs:5009`). The bumped thread schema is what refuses it first.
- **The store** goes from schema 35 to 36 with two table rebuilds: `issues.number` is the rowid, and `wps.seq` is an integer that would turn an all-digit id into a number.
- **The published faces** (JSON Schema, DDL, the GraphQL SDL) and the export bundle take a new version. They are ic's side of the contract, so they need both seats.
- **The new binary refuses a canon name of neither family by name.** The silent skip is a No Silent Errors defect that exists today.

### The merge (cc)

Hashed ids do not end the conflicts measured above, because two branches that each mint still each add a row to the same three files. ST0096 takes those three files out of git (hv decision 66), and this package keeps the merge exact for what stays in git.

- **`plan.rs` learns the hashed family.** Today `classify` sends any canon path that is not an ordinal to take-a-side, which discards one side's record (`plan.rs:608-708`). This lands in the same unit as the mint, never after it.
- **`.intentfiles` and the two aggregate views are no longer merged here.** ST0096 moves realisation into each record (cc's R1) and stops tracking the two lists, so in an upgraded project none of the three is in git. A branch cut before the upgrade runs `intent upgrade` before it merges, so a set merge would have no case left. cc dropped both on 2026-11-19, AC-05.2 is withdrawn, and issue 0704 is superseded by ST0096.
- **Two branches that each add a work package to one thread** have different ids, so both are kept with no repair and no moved claim.

### Criteria and tests (cc)

Their ids stay as the caller assigns them. **The group between the dash and the dot is the work package's id**, and four places read it: the close gate (`contract.rs:19-33`, `59-65`), `wp show` and `wp gate` (`facade.rs:5582-5590`), `acceptance.md` (`views.rs:1301-1318`) and `doctor` (`doctor.rs:820-830`, `1244-1258`, `1427-1431`). A door takes a prefix for the group and stores it whole.

**The riskiest site in the census is here.** When no criterion matches a package's group, the gate passes and rolls up to the thread's contract (`contract.rs:888-896`). One missed site would let `wp done` close a hashed package with none of its criteria judged.

### Doors, tables and views (ic)

- The CLI's parsers, the length rule, and prefix resolution at every door, with the ambiguity refusal.
- Two path grammars go through the type: `intent:///` and the navigator's `/thread/<id>/wps/<seq>` (`nav.rs:204-307`).
- GraphQL's `issue(number: Int!)`, `Issue.number` and `WorkPackage.seq` become `id: String!` with no alias, and a creation instant is added. The Swift app is the only client and moves in the same cut. MCP passes every id as a string already, so only its descriptions change.

## Upgrading a project, and the fleet

1. **Every machine that opens the project upgrades Intent first.** An older binary refuses the new canon by name, and stops there.
2. **`intent upgrade` once per project**, committed as one mechanical change. No id changes.
3. **An open branch upgrades before it merges.** The format migration is deterministic, so the merge is clean.
4. **`intent claude upgrade --apply` in each estate**, in the same visit as hv decision 41's sweep, so the hooks and `session-context.sh` re-render.
5. **The store migration is one way.** A brew 3.4.0 on the same machine refuses a store a newer build has migrated.

**A project not yet upgraded** (cc's meaning, 2026-11-19, put to hv as a change a user sees): the new build reads it and works on its ordinals as 3.4.0 does, and writes canon back in the project's own format, so nothing is rewritten behind the user's back and a machine still on 3.4.0 keeps working beside it. The first mint (`st new`, `wp new`, `issues add`, and the transition's re-mint) refuses and writes nothing, with `intent upgrade` as its one remedy. doctor names the upgrade as an advisory that is not counted. The format is one fact per project, the schema of `.canon/project.json`, which `intent upgrade` writes; 3.4.x already reads that file on every read of the disk and refuses an unknown schema by name, writing and deleting nothing, so it refuses an upgraded project whatever it holds. That closes risk 3.

**The store holds the format too** (cc's shape, 2026-11-20, from two reds in the suite of the unit that builds WP-05 and WP-06). The project table's `canon_format` (rung 36) carries the project canon's schema string, as the table already carries the todo cutoff. NULL reads as 3.4.0's format, as an absent file does, a rule stated once in `canon_format.rs`. `carry_project_state` carries it from disk: a present `project.json` sets it, and an absent one leaves the store's value. `Facade::canon_format` reads the store, and the projection writes `.canon/project.json` whenever the format is the release's. So an egest restores the file, and a deleted one comes back at the next write. A checkout whose store is at the release's format and switches to a branch from before the upgrade keeps that format, and its next write re-encodes that branch's canon in it, as the store already writes back a record a branch lacks.

**While this is being built, that reaches the main checkout by itself** (dc's finding). The repository's own commit gate runs the dev binary's `doctor` on the store of the checkout that is committing (`bin/.devbin/cmd/precommit:302-330`, `thread_view_skew_check.sh:84`), and every seat shares that build target. Once the shared target holds a binary with the new store schema, the next commit in the main checkout migrates the main store, and brew 3.4.0, first on every PATH, then refuses it: every `intent wb` verb and both hook carriers. So the first thing dc builds is a gate that judges a copy of the store whenever the build's store schema is newer than the store's. With that in place the packages land on main one at a time, as usual. A build is still never run by hand against the main checkout, and a worktree has its own store.

## Risks, the silent ones first

1. **A hashed work package closes with its criteria unjudged** (the gate's roll-up, above). It does not ship without a test of exactly that.
2. **A merge discards a hashed record** if the mint lands before `plan.rs` knows the family.
3. **Brew 3.4.0 deletes a hashed issue** in a project that has no thread to refuse on. Every project with one thread is protected by the schema bump.
4. **The brew smoke goes red after the release is public.** It is fixed before the rehearsal.
5. **Mixed versions across the fleet**: `.intentfiles` fails open in an older build, which then realises everything.
6. **Search**: how the stemmer treats a hex token is an inference, not a run. cc checks it before search is relied on for ids.
